The Academy of Arts is the Art esfera’s institution of higher education in Laerta. Time here is marked by a tower: figures of the mirnas move along a circular balcony, and when the fertility mirna Vinsenya emerges beneath the enameled sun, it means that it is about two in the afternoon.

Alvaro’s lectures (ch. 3, 13)

In the literature lecture hall, its walls hung with quotations from the classics, Alvaro teaches a series entitled “The Protagonist” (ch. 3). He adds poverty to his list of a hero’s attributes: a rich man inspires envy, a needy man is relatable to the reader, and a well-fed man wants nothing. The student in the front row with a golden fountain pen—Beatriz—argues with him, while a yellow-haired Reformist student (Wasp) thanks him for his speech in the Chamber of the Word. Alvaro goes to the dean of the faculty of letters, Don Farmiga, to ask for an advance, but is refused: he drank away the previous advance and still owes five lectures. The dean threatens to replace him with the poet Cecilia Armani. In chapter 13, the series ends with a lecture on a hero’s flaws, which Alvaro delivers listlessly and without preparation.

Other episodes (ch. 11–24)

In chapter 11, Alvaro gets rid of his persistent pupil Beatriz by writing to her father; in chapter 16, an important conversation takes place behind Jose Flarbo’s bookshop near the academy; in chapter 24, after a lecture, he leaves with Beatriz in her car. Nearby stands the Academy of Sciences, which once invited van Halm to join it.
